metadata.description: The nested case, and the widest one in the workspace. dist/packages/dbx-cli is ONE npm package with 12 entry points, not 12 packages: five rollup subpaths (dbx-cli-manifest-extract, -route, -eslint, -model-test, -test) and seven esbuild CLI bundles (-firebase-api-manifest, -lint-cache, -generate-firestore-indexes, -firestore-query-manifest, -generate-mcp-manifest, -generate-route-manifest, -validate) all compile INTO this directory and are named by this package's own dist `exports` and `bin`. So this target is the sole deliverable and the sole owner of the directory.  What changed: the thirteen sequential `npx nx run <child>:build-base` shell-outs became dependsOn EDGES. Each of those was a separate Nx process with its own task graph, so nothing deduped and `parallel: false` was the only ordering; now it is one process, one graph, and Nx schedules the children by their real layering (3 waves: dbx-cli:build-base; the ten children that need only it; then -firebase-api-manifest and -validate, which also need the -manifest-extract / -model-test siblings) instead of 13 sequential steps. The finalize stays this target's own command, so it runs after every entry point is built -- dependsOn does not order its own entries, which is exactly why the post-step must not be a sibling list item, and why every child carries its own explicit edge to `dbx-cli:build-base` rather than relying on this list's order.  The seven esbuild children also LOST the `build` targets they used to carry: each shelled out to its own `build-base`, which this target's command list already ran, so those subprojects were built twice into the same directory on every `nx build dbx-cli`.  Outputs stay the whole directory, which is correct HERE precisely because this task is its only writer: the cache payload is always complete, so the restore that remove()s the directory always puts all of it back. `inputs` has to name the nested project directories explicitly -- `production` resolves `{projectRoot}/**/*` against this project's OWN file list, which Nx assigns nested projects' files away from, so without these globs a child's source change would not invalidate the cached copy of the directory that child writes into.

`^build`, NOT the `^build-base` @nx/rollup/plugin infers. @nx/js remaps @dereekb/* imports to the dist DIRECTORY, so TypeScript reads that directory's package.json `exports` to resolve them -- and rollup writes `.` as {import, types} until that dependency's own `build` reorders it. `^build-base` would compile this package against un-finalized dependencies.  `^build` here also walks the pre-existing dbx-cli <-> dbx-cli-firestore-indexes project-graph cycle (this package imports @dereekb/dbx-cli/firestore-indexes; that project reaches back into packages/dbx-cli/src/lib/scan-helpers by relative path). It does NOT become a task-graph cycle: dbx-cli-firestore-indexes has no `build`, so Nx creates a dummy task, and filterDummyTasks (create-task-graph.js) drops the deps of any dummy that sits on a cycle -- so the dummy's would-be edge back to dbx-cli:build is discarded. Nothing is lost by that: its only other dep, util, is already a real edge here. Verified with createTaskGraph + findCycle over 12 scenarios before this change landed.
